questions.question: Point P and Q are 400 km apart. A person starts from P towards Q at 6 a.m. at a speed of 20 km/h. Another person starts from Q towards P at 6:30 a.m. at a speed of 30 km/h. At what time will they meet?

questions.question: 8 girls and 12 boys can complete a piece of work in 4 days, while 10 girls and 6 boys can complete it in 6 days. How long will 5 girls and 3 boys take to complete this same piece of work?
questions.solution:
Given: 

8 girls and 12 boys can complete a piece of work in 4 days

10 girls and 6 boys can complete it in 6 days

Concepts used:

Time = Work/Efficiency

Calculation:

Let the work efficiency of 1 boy be B and the work efficiency of 1 girl be G.

Work = Efficiency × Time

⇒ Total work by 8 girls and 12 boys = (8G + 12B) × 4 = 32G + 48B

⇒ Total work by 10 girls and 6 boys = (10G + 6B) × 6 = 60G + 36B

As total work remains the same,

⇒ 32G + 48B = 60G + 36B

⇒ 48B – 36B = 60G – 32G

⇒ 12B = 28G

⇒ B/G = 7/3

Total work = 32G + 48B = 32 × 3 + 48 × 7 = 432

 The efficiency of 5 girls and 3 boys = 5 × 3 + 3 × 7 = 36

Time = Work/Efficiency

⇒ 432/36 = 12

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: A man takes 4 hours and 30 minutes to row a boat a distance of 18 km downstream, and 3 hours 30 minutes to row the boat a distance of 7 km upstream. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

When the boat is going upstream, its effective speed is (a - b) km/hr.

When the boat is going downstream, its effective speed is (a + b) km/hr. 

distance = speed x time

**Calculation:**

Let's assume that the speed of the boat in still water is 'a' km/hr and the speed of the stream is 'b' km/hr.

The distance traveled downstream is 18 km. We know that the time taken to cover this distance downstream is 4 hours and 30 minutes, which is 4.5 hours.

18 = (a + b) x 4.5

Simplifying the equation, we get:

⇒ a + b = 4

The distance traveled upstream is 7 km. We know that the time taken to cover this distance upstream is 3 hours and 30 minutes, which is 3.5 hours.

Using the distance formula,

⇒ 7 = (a - b) x 3.5

Simplifying the equation, we get:

⇒ a - b = 2

We now have two equations with two variables. We can solve these equations simultaneously to find the values of 'a' and 'b'.

Adding the two equations, we get:

⇒ 2a = 6

⇒ a = 3

Substituting the value of 'a' in one of the equations, we get:

⇒ 3 - b = 2

⇒ b = 1

**Therefore, the speed of the stream is 1 km/hr.**

questions.question: The core of the Great Himalayas is composed of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Granite**__.

The Great Himalayas, also known simply as the Himalayas, stretch across five countries: Bhutan, India, Nepal, China, and Pakistan. They form the planet’s highest mountain range and are home to some of the world's tallest peaks, including Mount Everest. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The core of the Great Himalayas, being the result of such colossal tectonic forces, is primarily composed of metamorphic and igneous rocks, due to the immense pressure and heat generated by the collision of the continental plates.

 

 
• **Granite**, an igneous rock, is found extensively in the crust of the Earth and forms a significant part of the continental crust. Granite is formed from the slow cooling of magma underground. Due to the intense tectonic activities and the melting of the crust in certain areas, granite is indeed one of the key components of the core of the Great Himalayas.

**Therefore, the core of the Great Himalaya is mainly composed of granite. Hence, option 2) granite is the correct answer.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The presence of granite and other igneous and metamorphic rocks in the core of the Great Himalayas is a testament to the dynamic earth processes. 
 
• These processes are not only responsible for forming mountains but also influence climate patterns, biodiversity, and human cultures in the region.
 
• The study of the Himalayas' geology offers valuable insights into past plate tectonic movements and helps in understanding the potential for future seismic activity in this seismically active region.

questions.question: Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth is lower than ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __5.5__.

__
 
• Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth is lower than 5.5.
 
• Tooth enamel, made up of calcium phosphate is the hardest substance in the body. 
 
• It does not dissolve in water but is corroded when the pH in the mouth is below 5.5.
 
• Bacteria present in the mouth produce acids by the degradation of sugar and food particles remaining in the mouth after eating.
 
• The best way to prevent this is to clean the mouth after eating food.
 
• At the pH of 5.5, the teeth risk of cavities and tooth decay begins in the mouth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The role of toothpaste to prevent tooth decay is as follows-
 
 
• A healthy mouth is in a neutral pH range. Teeth can actually become stronger and re-mineralize when the pH of the mouth is 7.5 or above.
 
• Bacteria present in the mouth produce acids by the degradation of sugar and food particles remaining in the mouth after eating.
 
• Using toothpaste, which is generally basic, for cleaning the teeth can neutralize the excess acid and prevent tooth decay.
 
• Fluoride is a mineral that can prevent tooth decay from progressing. It can even reverse or stop, early tooth decay. Hence most of the toothpastes have fluoride ions.
 
• Also, tooth-pastes have salts in them which decreases the acidity of mouth.
